summary: Tompkins County, NY: CCC-built steel fire tower on Blackman Hill, in service April 1941; moved to the State Fairgrounds in the early 1980s; FFLA lists the original site as gone.

facts.design: Steel tower with stairway to a glass-enclosed cab; a 1940 item gives 75 feet and a 1941 item gives 68 feet
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the Blackman Hill site as Tower Gone; the tower now stands at the State Fairgrounds as part of a DEC exhibit
facts.agency: New York State Conservation Department chose the site; built by CCC enrollees from Camp SP-125

access.note: Part of a permanent DEC exhibit at the New York State Fairgrounds, per DEC. Sources read do not say whether the cab can be entered.

events.note: Built by CCC enrollees from Camp SP-125 on Blackman Hill in the Town of Caroline; a 1940 Ithaca Journal item gives 75 feet
Russell J. Boyer of Slaterville Springs appointed observer for the spring fire season as the tower went into operation; a 1941 item gives 68 feet
Removed to the State Fairgrounds in the early 1980s (no exact year in the Ithaca Journal account); now part of a permanent DEC exhibit
CNY Hiking's list gives the move to the NY State Fair as 1985

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1940 Ithaca Journal item gives 75 feet and the 1941 item gives 68 feet, both quoted on the Forest Lookouts page. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one.
The Ithaca Journal account quoted by Forest Lookouts says the early 1980s; CNY Hiking's list gives 1985. Left as a disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Built and first-observer facts rest on two 1940-1941 newspaper items quoted by Forest Lookouts; no later primary source found. The DEC and FFLA list agree the tower is at the fairgrounds. Original-record coordinates (42.36463, -76.26985) are roughly a kilometre from the DEC Blackman Hill Road parking area (42.356657, -76.26149); not checked against the tower footprint. A 1940 elevation (1,800 ft) and 1941 elevation (1,920 ft) differ; elevation is not in the story. No fire events in the sources read.
